explanation: The low-fidelity model changes heading instantaneously, ignores wind and acceleration, and uses constant power. The high-fidelity demonstrative point-mass model integrates velocity, acceleration limits, wind disturbance, idle power, and speed-dependent power. These differences can change trigger time, landing time, distance traveled, and energy use; neither fidelity is asserted physically correct without validation data.
